title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-response-format-openai-compat
author: Sofia Park
description:
Summary: Add a JSON Schema-based structured output mode to the Response Format API with a strict validation option and improved error reporting; include an OpenAI-compatibility adapter for the response_format parameter.

Context and motivation: Customers want deterministic, machine-parseable model outputs. We already support a lightweight response_format for structured output; this PR implements a formally validated JSON Schema mode that can be toggled via response_format.schema with a strict flag. When strict=true the runtime will validate model output against the supplied schema and return structured error details when validation fails. The implementation also includes an OpenAI-compat mapping so existing openai-style response_format usage transitions cleanly.

What this PR does:
- Add jsonschema validation path in the API layer (response_format.handler) and a runtime validator that runs in the streaming and non-streaming code paths.
- Implement strict mode semantics: with strict=true we refuse to return partially-valid outputs and instead return a structured validation error (error type: jsonschema_validation_failed) with error locations, top-level error message, and suggested fallback.
- Improve error payloads: include snippet context, expected vs actual types where available, and a unique validation_hint to help correlation in logs.
- Add OpenAI-compat adapter: translate legacy response_format.openai_schema into our internal schema format and preserve their "strict" semantics while adding richer error metadata.
- Backward compatibility: default behavior is non-strict (best-effort extraction). Existing clients that do not opt into strict mode see no behavior change.
- Docs, tests and examples: add API docs for response_format.schema, examples for strict vs non-strict, and an end-to-end test harness that exercises streaming and non-streaming flows.

Design notes:
- Validation is performed after tokenization-decoding in the streaming path at defined commit points to avoid excessive latency; the validator can return a soft-fail (non-strict) or hard-fail (strict) result.
- To preserve latency SLOs we added a size guard and a timeout to schema validation; if validator times out in strict mode we return a validation_timeout error with telemetry hooks to surface affected requests.
- Error messages are intentionally machine-friendly: error_type, validation_hint, path (JSON pointer), message, snippet. Human-readable message also present for SRE and UX.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation for API and runtime validator
- [x] OpenAI compatibility adapter and mapping tests
- [x] Unit tests for error payloads and parsing edge cases
- [x] Integration tests for streaming + strict mode
- [x] Docs and examples updated (docs/api/structured_output.md)
- [x] Added e2e test harness with simulated model mis-formatting

Testing & CI: Local unit and integration suite added. CI had one flaky e2e run on initial push (streaming test), re-run passed. Load-tested validator on internal perf-canary with no measurable regression for non-strict traffic; strict-mode validation increases tail latencies for affected requests (documented in release notes).

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and API opt-in. We will rollout to beta customers first (internal flag + metadata) and monitor validation error rates and latency impact. If telemetry shows unexpected user impact we will provide a non-blocking warning mode as follow-up.

Related: ENG-4120 schema validation design doc, ENG-4221 openai-compat mapping.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the streaming integration (response_format.streaming.commit_point) and the shape of the error payload for strict mode. We included a compatibility shim to keep OpenAI-style usage unchanged unless strict=true.

Release notes: 
- Add JSON Schema based structured output support via response_format.schema; supports strict validation which returns jsonschema_validation_failed with structured error details.
- OpenAI compatibility adapter for response_format.openai_schema.
- Added telemetry (validation_hint) to help map errors to schema and model output.
commits: Initial response_format schema plumbing and handler
Add jsonschema validator, strict mode handling and timeout guards
OpenAI compatibility adapter and mapping tests
Docs and e2e tests for streaming + strict mode
review_comments: Ethan Zhao: Left a comment about the validator timeout default (30ms looks aggressive) - we should make it configurable per-customer or tied to plan tier.
Sofia Park: Updated to make timeout configurable via runtime flags and added per-customer override in Dedicated/Private deployments.
Maya Patel: Can we make the validation_hint deterministic across retries? It's important for deduping errors in observability.
Sofia Park: Yes - validation_hint is now a stable hash of schema_id + pointer + truncated model output snippet; added unit tests.
Ravi Singh: Compatibility adapter looks good, but please add a note in docs about differences in error codes vs OpenAI.
Sofia Park: Added note to docs/api/structured_output.md comparing our error structure to OpenAI's and mapping guidance for clients.
ci_checks: e2e streaming: flaky on first run -> re-run -> pass
notes: Opt-in API feature behind runtime flag; non-strict default preserves existing behavior for backward compatibility.
release_notes:
- JSON Schema structured output via response_format.schema with optional strict validation (jsonschema_validation_failed error)
- OpenAI compatibility adapter for response_format.openai_schema
- New telemetry: validation_hint (useful to correlate validation failures with model outputs)
user_impact: Low by default (non-strict). Beta customers using strict mode may see validation failures when models produce slightly malformed output; documented mitigation and fallback guidance included in docs.
